text: A one-page website for "Brew Lab", a small specialty coffee shop in Indiranagar, Bengaluru.Visitors should see the menu with prices, the opening hours, and where to find us, and be able to pre-order a coffee for pickup. It should feel warm and modern and work well on a phone. Include a section about our beans and the farms they come from, and a simple loyalty-card explainer (buy 9, get the 10th free).

@CEO Before I write the charter I need three decisions the brief leaves open. Budget is 100. A baseline build (menu, hours, location, beans, loyalty, pre-order form, cart interaction, styling) costs about 80 on the rate card, leaving 20 for fixes.
1. Pre-order mechanics: the site is one static file with no server, so it cannot take or store orders. Option A: the form builds the order and opens a prefilled WhatsApp message to the shop; payment at pickup; no cost to run, but the shop must confirm manually and needs a WhatsApp number from the Requester. Option B: the form shows an on-page confirmation only and sends nothing; simplest, but customers may believe an order was placed when it was not, which is a false promise. We recommend A. Choose A or B?
2. Content facts: real prices, hours, address and farm names exist only with the Requester. Option A: build now with clearly marked placeholder content and have the Requester confirm or replace it at the end; faster, but risks wrong prices or invented farm claims going live if not replaced. Option B: pause now and ask the Requester for the facts first; slower, but no false claims. We recommend A, with placeholders visibly labeled and farm sourcing left generic until confirmed. Choose A or B?
3. Language and budget: Option A: English only, about 80 spent, about 20 held for two fixes (8 each). Option B: add Kannada (12), about 92 spent, room for one fix only. The brief names no language need. We recommend A. Choose A or B?

@Identity Go with A on all three; your recommendations stand. The brief is silent on each, so I picked the simplest option that avoids a false promise.
1. 1. A: the form builds the order and opens a prefilled WhatsApp message, with payment at pickup. The page must say the order is confirmed only when the shop replies. The WhatsApp number is a labeled placeholder until the Requester supplies it. I chose this because the brief is silent on mechanics and B would mislead customers.
2. 2. A: build now with visibly labeled placeholder prices, hours, address and WhatsApp number. Keep farm and bean sourcing generic, with no invented farm names or claims. Track these as open inputs for the Requester; they do not block done.
3. 3. A: English only, about 80 spent, about 20 held for two fixes. The brief names no language need, and Kannada can be added later if the Requester asks.

@Adaptation Charter is recorded with the CEO's three rulings built in. Propose workflows within the 100 budget: the baseline is about 80 (5 sections, 1 form, 1 cart feature, styling), with 20 held for two fixes. Propose the smallest set that closes every done-when item.
@Adaptation Charter valid: statement present, 13 checkable done-when items. Work can start.

@Priority Two workflows, total 80, leaving 20 held for two fixes. W1 builds the file with the five content sections and styling (55). W2 adds the pre-order form and cart script to that file (25). Trade-off: splitting adds a hand-off, but it lets Audit check the static content before the WhatsApp logic goes in.

proposal.name: Brew Lab page shell, content sections and styling
proposal.goal_gap: No file exists. Nothing shows menu, hours, location, beans and farms, or loyalty content.
proposal.expected_outcome: One HTML file with a viewport meta tag, a warm responsive style with a modern font stack, and English-only sections for menu, opening hours, location, beans and farms, and loyalty. Menu has several items, each with a price labeled as a placeholder. Hours and the Indiranagar, Bengaluru address are labeled placeholders. Beans text is generic with no named farm or region. Loyalty states buy 9, get the 10th free. A visible list shows which details are still placeholders.
outputs: brewlab.html (static sections, inline CSS, placeholder list)
proposal.completion_check: File has separate menu, hours, location, beans and farms, and loyalty sections. Every menu price and the hours and address are labeled placeholders. The loyalty text contains 'buy 9' and '10th free'. The beans section names no farm or region. A viewport meta tag and a media query or fluid layout are present. The CSS defines coffee or cream tones and a font stack. The placeholder list is visible.

proposal.name: Pre-order form with WhatsApp order builder
proposal.goal_gap: Visitors cannot pre-order. The file has no form or script to build a WhatsApp message.
proposal.expected_outcome: A pre-order section in the same file with item and quantity pickers and a name field. A script builds the order text and opens a wa.me link with the text prefilled. The WhatsApp number is a labeled placeholder in one clearly marked constant. Near the form, the page says payment is at pickup and that the order is confirmed only when the shop replies.
outputs: brewlab.html (pre-order section, inline JS, WhatsApp number constant)
proposal.completion_check: Pre-order section has item and quantity inputs and a name field. The script builds order text and opens a wa.me or api.whatsapp.com URL with encoded text. The number is defined once in a marked constant and labeled as a placeholder. Text near the form says payment is at pickup and the order is confirmed only when the shop replies. The page still has no horizontal scroll at phone width.

@Identity All 13 done-when items are met on a read of the code, with 3 warnings. I did not render the page or run the script, so items 6 and 10 rest on code and spec reading, not a test. Warning 1 (medium): window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener') returns null by spec, so the fallback window.location.href = url also runs. A visitor likely gets a new WhatsApp tab and the page itself navigates away. This is unverified in a browser. A fix fits the 8 reserve, but it is your call whether it is worth spending before the Requester review. Warning 2 (medium, low confidence): .ph uses white-space: nowrap and body has overflow-x: hidden. At about 320px the hours table cell may overflow its card and be clipped, not scrolled. This is my estimate, not a measurement. Warning 3 (low): the beans text says 'ground and brewed to order' and 'we choose beans with that in mind', which are small unconfirmed claims, and the placeholder number is written twice in the script (WHATSAPP_NUMBER and PLACEHOLDER_NUMBER). Neither breaks a criterion.

Done-when holds. Audit reports all 13 items PASS on a code read, with no failing items. Three warnings do not break any criterion. Two caveats: the page was not rendered or run, so the WhatsApp script and phone-width fit rest on code reading. The window.open noopener fallback may open a tab and also navigate the page away; this is unverified. Open inputs (real prices, hours, address, WhatsApp number, farm facts, language) stay open and do not block done. They go to the Requester with the review, and the 20 reserve is still available for two fixes if the Requester wants the warnings fixed.

Done: Identity confirmed every done-when item holds, with Audit's evidence. Open inputs for the Requester (not blocking): Real menu items and prices; Real opening hours; Real street address and map location; Shop WhatsApp number for pre-orders; Real bean details, farm names and sourcing facts; Whether Kannada or any other language is wanted later. Site v2 is in the preview. Requester: tell us if you want changes.
